doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Interview method and how he opens an interview
summary: He uses a tape recorder and asks about family and beginnings, as with Joe Wilder's father the bass player.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Opening the interview: introductions, date and place

blocks.x: Just from a — I can’t think of the word here — logistical sense, when you do that are you sitting and writing? Are you just taking notes?
You have a little tape recorder? Is that how you do it?
Okay. Do you have a favorite line to get people started? Because if you do maybe I’ll borrow it.

Um, I think really I just sort of say look, I really want to talk about your start in things, can we go right back. “Well you mean right back?” Yeah let’s go back as far as you want to go. Let’s just talk about your family life and how things started. Give me a little picture of your family circumstances. Something like that. And most people will paint you a little picture of where they lived, maybe the kind of environment their parents were part of, you know, and then usually you’ll sort of get into well where did music sort of come into the picture. Like Joe was telling me today you see, his father was, I didn’t know this, a professional bass violin player. He started on the cornet, went to the sousaphone. So he was telling me all about that and the bands that his father played, and that sort of opened up how he came to be involved in music. And you know it leads on from there.
When you are at a festival like this and I was observing you just tonight taking notes.
